newsitem.title: UK: Hambros says banking returns inadequate.
newsitem.headline: Hambros says banking returns inadequate.

text.p: British investment banking and financial services group Hambros Plc said on Wednesday the return on capital earned by its banking group was still inadequate.
But the bank's chief executive, Sir Chips Keswick, said in the group's results statement that despite this it had made progress towards its medium-term objectives in each main area of activity.

Hambros said the improvement in its pre-tax profit to 64.7 million stg for the year to March 31 had been largely attributable to the performance of its estate agent group Hambro Countrywide but also to the banking group where exceptional costs were reduced to 9.0 million stg from 12.2 million stg.
Pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit for the banking group rose to 10.2 million stg from 0.5 million stg.

"Whilst we had hoped that the profitability of the banking group would be restored more quickly, we remain convinced of the prospects and opportunities for an independent medium-sized bank providing advice and service to its clients in selected fields of competitive strength," Hambros' chairman Lord Hambro said in his letter to shareholders.
Hambros said it would pay a final dividend of 5.0 pence per share, making a total of 7.5 pence for the year, unchanged on the previous year.
